text:
maria: :rotating_light: pager triggered for org-4932 — spike in requests getting 429s and auth rejections from rl-gateway. Observed 5xxs rising at 02:04 UTC, P50 latency up 3x. Paging SRE oncall.

pagerduty: Incident created • Severity: P1 • Assigned: aj (SRE oncall) • Incident ID: INC-2055-org4932

aj: ack — I'm on it. Looking at rl-gateway logs and quota service. Can someone drop the last 10m of request hashes?

maria: sharing quick query: 
``` 
# top-rate-origins last_10m
SELECT origin, count(*) as q FROM requests WHERE org_id='org-4932' AND status in (429,500) GROUP BY origin ORDER BY q DESC LIMIT 10;
```
results: one internal batch job (job-runner-7) accounts for 72% of excess QPS, repeated replays.

samir: confirm — the customer's integration started a retry loop after a downstream timeout; they ramped parallelism last deploy. I DM'd their SRE to pause.

aj: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase org quota to absorb legitimate traffic 2) enable short burst window so in-flight batches finish 3) add a per-connection backoff rule in routing to slow the offending origin 4) monitor costs. Who can approve a temp quota bump?

leah: growth ok from product side to allow a short-term bump — they are on enterprise plan and customer-facing. Approve for 30m.

aj: executing emergency change now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl org update-quota --org_id org-4932 --qps 60 --burst 180 --ttl 30m --reason "emergency mitigation: spike from job-runner-7"
```

ops-bot: ⚙️ running: redwoodctl org update-quota ...
ops-bot: ✅ success — quota set: qps 10 -> 60, burst 30 -> 180, TTL 30m, change_id=chg-2055-7ef

aj: change applied. Note: this increases token spend if traffic persists. I'm also applying a routing override to add per-origin cooldown for job-runner-7.

maria: adding quick routing rule: 
```
# routing override
redwoodctl routing set-cooldown --origin job-runner-7 --org org-4932 --cooldown 15s --reason monitoring_backoff
```
ops-bot: ✅ routing override applied.

samir: customer responded — they paused the job. Errors trending down. 429s dropped 80% in 4m. p95 latency back to baseline.

aj: good. Monitoring graphs: p50 latency back to 1.1x baseline, errors ~2%. Keeping temp quota for now, will auto-revert at TTL (30m) unless we extend. We'll leave the routing cooldown and keep watch.

leah: thanks. Please capture audit for billing so customer success can explain cost delta. Also create a follow-up to recommend a dedicated capacity slot if they need sustained throughput.

aj: creating follow-ups: INC-2055 follow-ups: (1) postmortem + timeline (owner: aj) (2) customer debrief w/CS (owner: leah) (3) entitlement review for org-4932 for dedicated capacity (owner: samir).

maria: small note — edge cache miss pattern suggested repeated identical prompts; added temporary KV prefix cache for org-4932 to reduce token regen. Applied: 
```
redwoodctl cache enable-prefix --org org-4932 --prefix="/v1/generate" --ttl 60s
```
ops-bot: ✅ cache rule enabled.

aj: timeline: 02:04 pager -> 02:07 quota bump applied -> 02:11 routing cooldown -> 02:15 KV cache enabled -> 02:38 errors within normal range.

samir: root cause summary (draft): customer-side runaway retries after downstream timeout + unexpected parallelism after a deploy. Mitigation worked; recommend 1) rate-limits per origin by default, 2) deployment safety limits on partner jobs, 3) offer dedicated capacity.

leah: agreed. I'll schedule the customer sync. If we see a pattern repeat, we'll propose a reserved capacity pilot.

aj: closing loop here for oncall: I'll let the TTL expire and monitor. If errors climb before TTL, I'll re-open and escalate. Otherwise I'll post an update when TTL auto-reverts.

ops-bot: Audit log: chg-2055-7ef applied by aj at 2055001290; TTL expires at 2055003090.

aj: TTL expired, quotas reverted to qps 10 at 2055003090. Monitoring shows stable traffic. Closing incident.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2055-org4932 resolved by aj.

maria: thanks all — postmortem task created and assigned.

leah: :thumbsup: good handling.

samir: filing a follow-up RFC for per-origin defaults.

aj: signing off from oncall.
